slot.brief: Solve a basic trig equation like sin x = -1/2 or 2cos^2 x = 1 and state the general solution in terms of n and π

stem: The general solution of $\tan 2x = \cot x$ is (where $n \in I$):
notes: from question bank gfa2ac9db28b3 (verified in job 20261127-115414-780e)
working:
$\tan 2x = \cot x = \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)$
$\Rightarrow 2x = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2} - x$
$\Rightarrow 3x = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow x = \frac{n\pi}{3} + \frac{\pi}{6}$
Check domain: $\cos 2x \neq 0$, $\sin x \neq 0$; the solution family never makes these zero, so it is the full valid set.

Independent check: Use cot x = tan(π/2 − x). Then 2x = π/2 − x + nπ, so x = π/6 + nπ/3.
solution: $\cot x=\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)$ and $\tan A=\tan B$ implies $A=B+n\pi$. Thus, $$2x=\frac{\pi}{2}-x+n\pi\quad\Rightarrow\quad x=\frac{n\pi}{3}+\frac{\pi}{6},\; n\in\mathbb Z.$$
